examples.en: At the moment there is no way to solve it.
I'm looking for a way to get the money.

examples.ko: 다른 방도는 없는지 다시 한번 알아볼게요.
examples.en: I'll check once more whether there's any other way.

examples.ko: 방도라도 알면 도와줄 텐데 저도 모르겠어요.
examples.en: I'd help if I knew any way at all, but I don't know either.
Time just passes with no good solution in sight.

examples.ko: 이 문제를 풀 방도를 함께 마련해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's work out a way to solve this problem together.

explain: '방법'과 비슷하지만 어려운 상황에서 문제를 해결할 길을 말할 때 주로 써요. '방도가 없다', '방도를 찾다·마련하다', '뾰족한 방도'처럼 굳어진 말이 많아요. 평범한 방법을 물을 때는 '방법'이 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The company worked out a way to solve the problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어려운 일을 풀 길을 준비한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means preparing a way to solve a difficult matter.

phrases.en: I still don't see any particular way out.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뾰족한 방도'는 보통 부정 표현과 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '뾰족한 방도' is usually used with a negative expression.

phrases.example: 다른 방도가 없어서 기다릴 수밖에 없었어요.
phrases.en: There was no other way, so I had no choice but to wait.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 해결 방법이 있는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about whether another solution exists.

explain_en: It is similar to '방법' but is mainly used for a way out of a difficult situation. Many set phrases exist, such as '방도가 없다', '방도를 찾다·마련하다' and '뾰족한 방도'. For asking about an ordinary method, '방법' sounds more natural.

dis.h: means or way out, usually in negatives
gh: practical way or steps to do something
established style or system of doing

p.n: 방법 is the everyday word; 방도 is more formal and mostly used with 없다 or 찾다.

t90.ax: I'm looking for a way to get the money.

examples.en: An unexpected dark horse showed up in the final.
The hidden danger in this exam is the English listening part.

examples.ko: 생각지도 못한 복병을 만나서 계획이 늦어졌어요.
examples.en: We ran into an unforeseen obstacle and the plan was delayed.

examples.ko: 이 팀은 이번 대회의 복병으로 꼽혀요.
examples.en: This team is regarded as the dark horse of this tournament.
The event was canceled because of the unexpected factor of the weather.

examples.ko: 복병처럼 숨어 있던 문제가 갑자기 드러났어요.
examples.en: A problem that had been lurking like a hidden trap suddenly came to light.

explain: 원래는 숨어서 기다리는 군사를 뜻하지만, 지금은 예상하지 못한 경쟁자나 장애물을 말할 때 많이 써요. 스포츠와 시험, 일 이야기에서 자주 나와요. '복병이 나타나다/숨어 있다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: An unexpected dark horse showed up in the final.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예상하지 못한 경쟁자가 등장할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an unexpected rival appears.

phrases.en: We hit an unexpected obstacle during construction, so it got delayed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일을 하다가 예상 밖의 장애물을 만났을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when running into an unexpected obstacle during work.

phrases.example: 쉬운 시험에도 복병이 숨어 있을 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Even an easy test can have a hidden catch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로 안 보이는 어려움이 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means there is a hidden difficulty not visible on the surface.

explain_en: It originally meant soldiers waiting in hiding, but now it mostly refers to an unexpected rival or obstacle. It often appears in talk about sports, exams and work. It is used as '복병이 나타나다' or '복병이 숨어 있다'.

en: to carry out; to execute; to put into action

examples.en: We made a plan, so let's carry it out now.
When you run the program, the screen turns on.
Don't just think about it; do it right away.
The team leader put the new policy into effect.
Start by setting a goal you can actually carry out.
I wrote the result of what I carried out in the report.

explain: '하다'보다 딱딱하고, 세운 계획이나 결정을 실제로 해 본다는 느낌이에요. 컴퓨터에서는 프로그램을 '실행하다'가 아주 자주 쓰여서 '실행 파일', '실행 버튼'을 볼 수 있어요. 비슷한 '실천하다'는 다짐이나 약속을 몸으로 옮길 때 어울려요.

phrases.example: 좋은 생각이 있으면 바로 실행에 옮겨요.
phrases.en: If I have a good idea, I put it into action right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각이나 계획을 실제 행동으로 바꾼다는 뜻의 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation meaning to turn an idea or plan into real action.

phrases.en: The program runs automatically.
phrases.nuance_ko: '실행하다'의 피동형으로, 사람이 아니라 프로그램이나 계획이 주어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Passive form; the subject is the program or plan, not a person.

phrases.en: If you press the run button, it starts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 컴퓨터나 앱 화면에서 자주 보는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase you often see on computer or app screens.

explain_en: Stiffer than 하다, it means actually carrying out a plan or decision. On computers 실행하다 is very common for running programs: you will see 실행 파일 and 실행 버튼. 실천하다 is similar but fits turning a resolution or promise into action.

examples.ko: 새 팀에서는 제 운신의 폭이 좁아요.
examples.en: On my new team, my room to maneuver is narrow.
I hurt my back, so even moving around is hard.
It's a small room, so there's no space to move around.
There were so many people that it was hard to move.

examples.ko: 비자 문제 때문에 운신에 제약이 많아요.
examples.en: Because of my visa situation, I have many limits on what I can do.
I'm so aware of people's eyes that I can't move freely.

explain: 혼자 쓰기보다 '운신의 폭', '운신이 어렵다'처럼 굳은 모양으로 많이 나와요. 몸을 움직이는 것뿐 아니라 어떤 일을 자유롭게 할 수 있는 범위를 말할 때도 써요. 말투가 딱딱해서 뉴스나 글에서 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.example: 계약 때문에 제 운신의 폭이 좁아졌어요.
phrases.en: to have little freedom to act
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 아니라 상황 때문에 할 수 있는 일이 제한될 때 비유로 써요. 반대는 '운신의 폭이 넓다'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively when circumstances, not the body, limit what you can do. The opposite is '운신의 폭이 넓다'.

explain_en: It is rarely used alone and mostly appears in set forms such as '운신의 폭' and '운신이 어렵다'. It can mean physically moving, but also how freely you can act in a situation. The tone is stiff, so you see it more in news and writing.

t90.ax: On my new team, my room to maneuver is narrow.

examples.ko: 죄송하지만 오늘은 참석 여부를 확답하기 어려워요.
examples.en: Sorry, but I can't give a definite answer today about attending.
The manager said he would give a definite answer by Monday.

examples.ko: 그는 질문에 확답하지 않고 웃기만 했어요.
examples.en: He didn't give a straight answer to the question and just smiled.

examples.ko: 가격을 확답한 뒤에 계약서를 보내 드릴게요.
examples.en: I'll send the contract after I confirm the price.

examples.ko: 먼저 가족과 상의해 보고 내일 확답할게요.
examples.en: I'll talk with my family first and give you a firm answer tomorrow.
Now that I've given my word, I have to keep the promise.

explain: 그냥 '대답하다'가 아니라 분명하고 확실하게 답한다는 점이 달라요. 그래서 뒤에 책임이 따르는 느낌이 있어요. '지금은 확답을 못 드리겠어요'는 정중하게 결정을 미룰 때 많이 써요.

phrases.en: Please give me a definite answer by tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '확답하다'를 '확답을 주다'로 풀어 말하면 부탁할 때 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Saying 확답을 주다 sounds natural when making a request.

phrases.en: I got a definite answer from that person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대의 분명한 대답을 들었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you have received a clear answer from someone.

phrases.en: I can't give you a definite answer right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결정을 정중하게 미룰 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to put off making a decision.

explain_en: Unlike plain '대답하다', it means answering clearly and firmly, so it carries a sense of responsibility afterward. '지금은 확답을 못 드리겠어요' is a polite way to put off a decision.

en: to be dark; to be darkish

examples.en: The banana peel has turned dark.
Your face has tanned darkish in the sun.
The sky turned dark and then it rained.
The area around my lips looked dark, so I went to the hospital.
The edges of the baked bread are darkish.
Dark clouds are rolling in.

explain: 완전히 검은 것이 아니라 '조금 검은' 정도일 때 써요. '검다'보다 약하고, 색이 변했거나 탔을 때 자주 어울려요. 같은 뜻의 '거무스레하다'도 있어요.

phrases.en: Clothes in a dark shade suit you well.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 형태로 명사를 꾸밀 때 쓰는 기본 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic modifier form used before a noun.

phrases.en: After being left out for a long time, the apple turned darkish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색이 조금 변했을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a color has changed a little.

phrases.en: The sky is turning dark.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어와 같은 뜻이고 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as the headword and interchangeable with it.

explain_en: It describes something not fully black but somewhat dark, weaker than '검다'. It suits things whose color has changed or tanned. There is also a near-identical form, '거무스레하다'.

examples.ko: 이 신발은 모양새는 투박해도 신으면 편해요.
examples.en: These shoes look clunky, but they are comfortable to wear.

examples.ko: 그렇게 싸우면 남 보기에 모양새가 안 좋아요.
examples.en: If you fight like that, it looks bad to others.

examples.ko: 오늘 회의는 아무 결정도 못 할 모양새예요.
examples.en: It looks like today's meeting won't decide anything.

examples.ko: 맛도 좋고 모양새도 예뻐서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: It tastes good and looks pretty, so it's popular.

examples.ko: 일이 돌아가는 모양새를 보니 쉽게 끝나지 않을 것 같아요.
examples.en: Judging by how things are going, it won't end easily.

examples.ko: 큰 회사가 작은 가게를 괴롭히는 모양새라서 비난이 커졌어요.
examples.en: It looked like a big company was bullying a small shop, so the criticism grew.

explain: '모양'이 눈에 보이는 생김새라면, '모양새'는 겉으로 보이는 꼴이나 상황이 남에게 어떻게 보이는지까지 말해요. '모양새가 좋다/안 좋다'처럼 평가할 때 많이 쓰고, '~는 모양새다'로 상황을 설명하기도 해요.

phrases.en: It doesn't look good if you leave on your own.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남에게 어떻게 보이는지 평가할 때 '좋다/안 좋다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 'good/bad' to judge how something looks to others.

phrases.en: The team has finally taken shape.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일이나 모임이 제대로 된 꼴이 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something finally takes proper shape.

phrases.en: It looks like the two companies are helping each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로 보이는 상황을 설명할 때 문장 끝에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Added at the end of a sentence to describe how a situation appears.

explain_en: '모양' is the shape or look you can see, while '모양새' also covers how a situation appears from the outside. It is often used to judge, as in '모양새가 좋다/안 좋다', and the pattern '~는 모양새다' describes how a situation looks.

t90.ax: If you fight like that, it looks bad to others.

examples.ko: 어머니는 생활력이 강해서 혼자서도 가게를 잘 꾸리세요.
examples.en: My mother is so resourceful that she runs the shop well even alone.

examples.ko: 생활력 있는 사람이랑 결혼하고 싶다고 친구가 말했어요.
examples.en: My friend said she wants to marry someone who can make a living.

examples.ko: 생활력은 나이와 상관없이 길러질 수 있어요.
examples.en: The ability to support yourself can be developed at any age.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 어려서부터 고생해서 생활력도 강하고 독립심도 커요.
examples.en: That child had a hard time from a young age, so he is both resourceful and independent.

examples.ko: 이 프로그램은 청년들의 생활력을 키우는 데 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: This program helps young people build the ability to support themselves.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 생활력에 감탄한 적이 많아요.
examples.en: I have often been amazed by that person's ability to get by.

explain: '생활력이 강하다'나 '생활력이 없다'처럼 돈을 벌고 살림을 꾸려 가는 힘을 말할 때 써요. 사람의 능력을 평가하는 말이라서 칭찬이 되기도 하고, '생활력이 없다'는 꽤 직접적인 비판으로 들릴 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 할머니는 생활력이 강하셔서 혼자서도 잘 사세요.
phrases.en: My grandmother has strong survival skills, so she lives well on her own.
phrases.nuance_ko: 칭찬할 때 쓰는 가장 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most typical pairing, used as praise.

phrases.example: 돈을 못 모으는 걸 보니 생활력이 없는 것 같아요.
phrases.en: Seeing that he can't save money, he seems to lack practical life skills.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비판으로 들릴 수 있으니 조심해서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This can sound like criticism, so use it with care.

phrases.example: 저는 생활력 있는 사람이 되고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to be a person who can take care of their own livelihood.
phrases.nuance_ko: '있는'으로 능력 있는 사람을 꾸며 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '있는' describes a capable person.

explain_en: It is used in '생활력이 강하다' or '생활력이 없다' for the power to earn money and run a household. Because it evaluates a person, it can be praise, while '생활력이 없다' can sound like quite direct criticism.

examples.ko: 성급히 결론을 내리지 말고 더 생각해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't jump to a conclusion; think about it more.
He hurriedly opened the door and went out.
I once judged too hastily and regretted it.
Don't give up too hastily.

examples.ko: 그녀는 성급히 대답하는 바람에 실수를 했어요.
examples.en: She answered in haste and ended up making a mistake.
I ate lunch too fast and got an upset stomach.

explain: '급히'는 서두르는 모습 자체를 말하지만, '성급히'는 차분히 생각하지 않고 서두른다는 안 좋은 느낌이 들어요. 일상 대화에서는 '성급하게'가 더 자연스럽고, '성급히'는 글이나 조언에서 잘 써요.

phrases.en: If you speak hastily, you might make a mistake.
phrases.nuance_ko: '성급히'와 뜻이 같고, 일상 대화에서는 이쪽이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 성급히, and more natural in everyday conversation.

phrases.en: A hasty decision is easy to regret later.
phrases.nuance_ko: '성급하다'의 활용형으로, 명사 앞에서 서두르는 나쁜 점을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form of 성급하다, pointing out the downside of rushing before a noun.

phrases.en: That person is too impatient.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 성격이 서두르는 편이라고 말할 때 쓰는 문장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A sentence for describing someone whose character tends to rush.

explain_en: '급히' just describes hurrying, but '성급히' carries a negative sense of rushing without thinking carefully. In daily talk '성급하게' sounds more natural, while '성급히' fits writing and advice.

examples.ko: 요즘 형편이 여의찮아서 여행은 못 가요.
examples.en: My finances are tight these days, so I can't go on a trip.
We provide support money to people in difficult circumstances.
If it isn't convenient for you, it's fine to come next time.
Things aren't going well, and I'm upset.

examples.ko: 지금은 시간이 여의찮은데 내일 얘기해도 될까요?
examples.en: I don't have the time right now, so can we talk tomorrow?
Their family situation seems difficult, and I'm worried.

explain: 형편, 사정, 일정이 뜻대로 되지 않을 때 돌려서 부드럽게 말하는 표현이에요. 정중하게 거절하거나 사정을 밝힐 때 '여의찮아서', '여의찮으시면'처럼 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 일정이 여의찮아서 이번 모임에는 못 가요.
phrases.en: My schedule isn't working out, so I can't go to this gathering.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거절하는 이유를 부드럽게 밝힐 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to give a reason softly when declining.

phrases.en: If it's not convenient for you, we can meet next time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대의 사정을 높여서 조심스럽게 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to politely ask about the other person's circumstances.

phrases.en: Even in difficult circumstances, I helped my younger sibling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이나 사정이 넉넉하지 않은 상황을 돌려 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A roundabout way to describe tight circumstances.

explain_en: It is a soft, indirect way of saying that your finances, circumstances or schedule are not working out as you'd like. It helps in politely declining or explaining a situation, as in '여의찮아서' and '여의찮으시면'.

t90.ax: Things aren't going well, and I'm upset.

en: to be complete; to be perfect

examples.en: This plan isn't complete yet.
Please answer in a complete sentence.

examples.ko: 그 설명은 완전해서 더 물어볼 게 없어요.
examples.en: The explanation is complete, so there is nothing more to ask.
No one can be perfect.
I check that the door is fully closed.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 선수가 다 모여서 완전해졌어요.
examples.en: The team became complete once all the players gathered.

explain: 빠진 것 없이 다 갖춰진 상태예요. 일상 대화에서는 부사 '완전'이 '완전 맛있어요'처럼 '아주'와 비슷하게 쓰여요. 이때는 '완전하다'로 활용하지 않고 '완전' 그대로 써요.

phrases.en: I need complete rest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '빠진 것 없는'의 뜻으로 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a noun to mean 'without anything missing'.

phrases.en: My explanation isn't complete yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금 부족하다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something is still lacking a bit.

phrases.en: I finished the homework completely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사로 '하나도 남김없이'라는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An adverb adding the sense of 'with nothing left over'.

explain_en: It describes a state where nothing is missing. In casual conversation the adverb '완전' is used like 'totally' or 'very', as in '완전 맛있어요'. In that use it does not conjugate; you say 완전, not 완전하다.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 위기에서도 침착성을 잃지 않았어요.
examples.en: That player didn't lose his composure even in a crisis.

examples.ko: 불이 났을 때는 침착성이 있는 사람이 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: When there's a fire, a person with composure is helpful.
My younger sibling lacks composure and often makes mistakes.
Appearing composed is important in an interview.

examples.ko: 아이들에게 침착성을 가르치는 일은 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: Teaching children to be composed is not easy.
Composure can be built up little by little with practice.

explain: 그 사람의 성격이나 태도를 말할 때 써요. 지금 이 순간의 모습은 '침착해요', '침착하게'가 더 자연스러워요. '침착성이 있다/없다/부족하다', '침착성을 잃다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I panicked and lost my composure.
phrases.nuance_ko: 평소의 차분함이 없어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone loses their usual calm.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is composed, so I trust them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 성격을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a person's character.

phrases.example: 저는 침착성이 부족해서 시험 때 실수를 해요.
phrases.en: I lack composure, so I make mistakes during exams.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부족한 점을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to point out a weakness.

explain_en: Use it for a person's character or general attitude. For how someone is right now, '침착해요' or '침착하게' is more natural. It appears as '침착성이 있다/없다/부족하다' and '침착성을 잃다'.

t90.ax: Teaching children to be composed is not easy.

en: to be even; to be flat

examples.en: This road is flat, so it is easy to walk.
They built a house on level ground.
That person's life was not smooth.
I am glad the work ended without trouble.
The path is level near the top of the mountain.
I heard it was easy, but it was quite hard.

explain: '평평하다'는 면이 고르다는 모양에 쓰고, '평탄하다'는 길이 고른 것 말고도 삶이나 일이 큰 어려움 없이 흘러가는 것에도 써요. 삶에는 '평탄하지 않았다'처럼 부정으로 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: It's a flat road, so it's good for cycling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때는 '평탄한'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '평탄한' when describing a noun that follows.

phrases.en: His life was not smooth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 삶이 어려웠다는 뜻으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to say that life was hard.

phrases.en: My parents have lived a smooth life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 어려움 없이 지낸 삶을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a life lived without major hardships.

explain_en: 평평하다 describes a surface that is even, while 평탄하다 also covers a life or task that goes along without big trouble. For life it is mostly used in the negative, as in '평탄하지 않았다' (it wasn't smooth).

t90.ax: That person's life was not smooth.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 현장감이 넘쳐서 실제 같아요.
examples.en: This movie is so vivid that it feels real.
You can feel the atmosphere just by looking at the photo.
The reporter described the situation vividly, as if on the spot.

examples.ko: 극장에서 보면 소리 때문에 현장감이 더 좋아요.
examples.en: In a theater, the sound makes it feel even more real.
The story felt so real that I listened closely.

examples.ko: 이 글은 현장감이 부족해서 읽기 지루해요.
examples.en: This text lacks vividness, so it's boring to read.

explain: '현장감이 있다', '현장감이 넘치다', '현장감이 살아 있다'처럼 칭찬할 때 자주 써요. 사진, 영상, 소리, 글이 마치 그 자리에 있는 것 같을 때 어울려요. '생생하다'와 같이 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: This photo has a sense of being there, so I like it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 자리에 있는 것 같다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as praise when it feels like you are on the spot.

phrases.en: The sound was loud in the theater, so I felt like I was there.
phrases.nuance_ko: 듣거나 보는 사람이 느끼는 감각을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes what the viewer or listener feels.
phrases.en_equiv: to feel a sense of realism

phrases.en: That article feels vivid, as if you were at the scene.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글이나 영상이 생생할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when writing or video feels vivid.

explain_en: It is often used as praise, as in '현장감이 있다', '현장감이 넘치다', and '현장감이 살아 있다'. It fits photos, video, sound, or writing that makes you feel you are right there. It also goes well with '생생하다' (vivid).
